h1: Find a public Bluesky profile by username
intro: Bluesky Profile Username Lookup starts with a candidate handle, but a matching string is only a lead. This Bluesky-focused page explains how to check the relevant profile, what a public result can and cannot show, and how to keep a possible match separate from an identity claim.

sections.heading: What a public Bluesky profile can show
sections.body: Use the official page to confirm the account type, current handle, and information the owner chose to publish. Bluesky handles can be domain-based and may change. Confirm the resolved profile and the handle shown on the service. A username result is a starting point for a self-audit or authorized review, not a complete record of the person behind an account.

sections.heading: Coverage and limits for Bluesky
sections.body: The checked-in MyRecon standard catalogue lists Bluesky. This is a username-level check, not a guarantee that every request will resolve: service changes, rate limits, privacy controls, or temporary blocks can leave a result unknown. A missing or blocked result cannot establish that no account exists. Do not work around login walls, access controls, rate limits, or service restrictions to force a response.

sections.heading: Verify a candidate before you rely on it
sections.body: Open the canonical Bluesky page, note the URL and observation date, and compare one or more independent details that are voluntarily public. A reused or renamed handle, a similarly named profile, a redirect, or a stale search snippet can create a false lead on Bluesky. Open the official destination and compare independent public context before attributing it to anyone. Keep uncertain and unavailable outcomes marked as unknown.

faq.question: Can a Bluesky username match prove who owns it?
faq.answer: No. Handles can be shared, changed, or reassigned. Open the public profile and look for independent, voluntarily published context before making an attribution; if evidence is inconclusive, leave the match unresolved.

faq.question: Does this find private Bluesky profiles?
faq.answer: No. This workflow is limited to supported checks and information available on public pages. Private accounts, login-only material, blocked requests, and hidden membership data are not exposed by a username lookup.

faq.question: What should I do if a Bluesky result is unavailable?
faq.answer: Record the check as unavailable or unknown, then use Bluesky's official search directly if appropriate. A timeout, redirect, or access block is not proof that the profile is absent.

platform.privacy_overview: A public Bluesky profile can show only the fields its owner and the service make visible, such as a chosen name, image, biography, posts, or outbound links. Private areas and access-controlled content are outside a public lookup.
platform.false_positive_note: A reused or renamed handle, a similarly named profile, a redirect, or a stale search snippet can create a false lead on Bluesky. Open the official destination and compare independent public context before attributing it to anyone.

manual_steps: Open https://bsky.app/ and use its own public profile search or the exact handle URL when the service documents one. Search only a username you own or are authorized to review; this guide does not cover private-account discovery.

Open the candidate profile page and confirm the destination is a current Bluesky account, not a generic error, unrelated result, or search-engine snippet. Save the canonical URL and the date if you need a reproducible self-audit.

Compare a separate, voluntarily public clue such as a self-linked site or matching biography before drawing a conclusion. A handle alone can be shared or reassigned, and blocked checks should stay unknown rather than being recorded as a negative.
